# HDonutChart

> A CSS-gradient ring summary with legend-driven inspection and exact amounts.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HDonutChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-donut-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthDonutChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HDonutChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- CSS conic-gradient ring, with no charting library. A central total, named legend buttons and exact-value table carry meaning beyond color. Inspection/selection is legend-driven, not slice hit-testing. Positive finite values contribute; at most 100 categories are shown. size defaults to 160px, thickness to 18px, and the ring fits its container.

## Public API

items: ChartSlice[] · label, selected, unit: string · size, thickness: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: ChartSlice[];
    label: string;
    selected?: string;
    unit?: string;
    size?: number;
    thickness?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [] }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, plot

Use `hearth-donut-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface ChartSlice extends ChartPoint {
    tone?: Tone;
}

export interface ChartPoint {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    value: number;
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HDonutChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HDonutChart label="Request mix" :items="[{id:'cached',label:'Cached',value:72},{id:'origin',label:'Origin',value:28}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-donut-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Request mix",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "cached",
      "label": "Cached",
      "value": 72
    },
    {
      "id": "origin",
      "label": "Origin",
      "value": 28
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
